[[File:Kugel-clelia-beisp.svg|thumb|upright=1.4|Clelia curves: floor plans of examples, arcs on the lower half of the sphere are dotted. The last four curves (spherical spirals) start at the south pole and end at the northpole. The upper four curves are due to the choice of parameter <math>c</math> periodic (see: [[Rose (mathematics)|rose]]).]]

In [[mathematics]], a '''Clélie''' or '''Clelia curve''' is a curve on a sphere with the property:<ref>{{citation|title=Modern Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces with Mathematica|first=Mary|last=Gray|edition=2nd|publisher=CRC Press|year=1997|isbn=9780849371646|page=928|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=-LRumtTimYgC&pg=PA928}}.</ref>
: If the surface of a sphere is described as usual by the [[longitude]]  (angle <math>\varphi</math>) and the [[colatitude]] (angle <math>\theta</math>) then 
::<math> \varphi=c\;\theta, \quad c>0</math>.

The curve was named by [[Luigi Guido Grandi]] after [[Celia Grillo Borromeo|Clelia Borromeo]].<ref>{{citation|title=Aperçu historique sur l'origine et le développement des méthodes en géométrie: particulièrement de celles qui se rapportent à la géométrie moderne, suivi d'un Mémoire de géométrie sur deux principes généraux de la science, la dualité et l'homographie|first=Michel|last=Chasles|language=French|authorlink=Michel Chasles|publisher=M. Hayez|year=1837|page=236|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XBkzAQAAMAAJ&pg=PA236}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|title=Histoire Des Mathématiques: Dans laquelle on rend compte de leurs progrès depuis leur origine jusqu'à nos jours : où l'on expose le tableau et le développement des principales découvertes dans toutes les parties des Mathématiques, les contestations qui se sont élevées entre les Mathématiciens, et les principaux traits de la vie des plus célèbres|first1=Jean Etienne|last1=Montucla|first2=Joseph Jérôme|last2=Le Français de Lalande|publisher=Agasse|year=1802|language=French|page=8|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2dJGAAAAcAAJ&pg=PA8}}</ref><ref>[http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Grandi.html McTutor Archive]</ref>

[[Viviani's curve]]  and [[spherical spiral]]s are special cases of Clelia curves. In practice Clelia curves occur as the [[ground track]] of [[satellite]]s in [[polar orbit|polar]] [[circular orbits]], i.e., whose traces on the earth include the poles. If the orbit is a [[Geosynchronous orbit|geosynchronous]] one, then <math> c=1 </math> and the trace is a Viviani's curve.

== Parametric representation ==
If the sphere of radius <math>r</math> is parametrized in the [[spherical coordinate system]] by
:<math>
\begin{align}
x &= r \cdot \cos \theta \cdot \cos \varphi \\
y &= r \cdot \cos \theta \cdot \sin \varphi \\
z &= r \cdot \sin \theta
\end{align}
</math>
where <math>\theta</math> and <math>\varphi</math> are angles, the longitude and latitude (respectively) of a point on the sphere
and these two angles are connected by a [[linear equation]] <math>\; \varphi=c\theta</math>, then using this equation to replace <math>\varphi</math> gives a parametric representation of a Clelia curve:
:<math>
\begin{align}
x &= r \cdot \cos \theta \cdot \cos c\theta \\
y &= r \cdot \cos \theta \cdot \sin c\theta \\
z &= r \cdot \sin \theta.
\end{align}
</math>

== Examples ==
Any Clelia curve meets the poles at least once.

'''Spherical spirals:''' <math>\quad c \ge 2 \ , \quad -\pi/2\le \theta\le \pi/2</math>

A spherical spiral usually starts at the south pole and ends at the north pole (or vice versa).

'''Viviani's curve:''' <math>\quad c=1\ , \quad 0 \le \theta\le 2\pi</math>

'''Trace of a polar orbit of a satellite:''' <math>\quad c\le 1\ ,\quad \theta\ge 0</math>

In case of <math>\;c\le 1\;</math> the curve is ''periodic'',  if <math>c</math> is [[Rational number|rational]] (see rose). For example: In case of <math>\; c=1/n\;</math> the period is <math>\;n\cdot 2\pi\;</math>. If <math>c</math> is a non rational number, the curve is not periodic.

The table (second diagram) shows the [[floor plan]]s of Clelia curves. The lower four curves are spherical spirals. The upper four are polar orbits. In case of <math>\;c=1/3\;</math> the lower arcs are hidden exactly by the upper arcs. The picture in the middle (circle) shows the floor plan of a Viviani's curve. The typical 8-shaped appearance can only be achieved by the projection along the x-axis.
